title: Quotient groups and the first isomorphism theorem
terms: quotient group; coset multiplication; first isomorphism theorem; factorization through a quotient.

exposition.text:
For a normal subgroup N ⊴ G, the quotient G/N consists of cosets, with (gN)(hN) = ghN.
Normality makes this independent of representatives. If G is finite, |G/N| = |G|/|N|. A homo-
∼
morphism φ : G → H induces an isomorphism G/ ker φ = im φ. Fibers of φ are cosets of its
kernel, so all nonempty fibers have the same size.
A homomorphism G → H factors through G/N exactly when it kills N . The quotient records
what remains after identifying elements whose ratio lies in N . A quotient of an abelian group is
abelian; a quotient being abelian does not force the original group to be abelian.

question.text:
Let G = (Z/12Z) × (Z/18Z) and N = ⟨(4, 6)⟩. What is the order of (1, 1) + N in G/N?
(A) 3 (B) 6 (C) 12 (D) 18 (E) 36

solution.text:
The subgroup is {(0, 0), (4,6), (8, 12)}. Membership of (k, k) requires k ≡ 4t (mod 12) and
k ≡ 6t (mod 18) for one t ∈ {0, 1, 2}. Compatibility modulo 6 requires 4t ≡ 0 (mod 6),
forcing t = 0. Thus k must be a multiple of both 12 and 18, whose least positive value is
36.

question.text:
How many homomorphisms φ : Z/24Z → Z/18Z have kernel of order 8?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 6

solution.text:
The image must have order 24/8 = 3. A map from a cyclic group is determined by the
image of 1, which must have order exactly 3. The two elements of order 3 in Z/18Z are 6
and 12, and both satisfy 24a = 0.

Let φ : Z → Z be φ(a, b) = 6a + 9b. To which group is Z / ker φ isomorphic?
2
(A) Z (B) Z/6Z (C) The trivial group (D) Z (E) Z/3Z

solution.text:
The image is 3Z, since the greatest common divisor of 6, 9 is three. The first isomorphism
theorem gives the quotient isomorphic to 3Z, which as an abstract additive group is isomor-
phic to Z, not to Z/3Z.

question.text:
Let φ : G → H be a homomorphism and N a normal subgroup of G contained in ker φ. The
induced map φ¯ : G/N → H is injective exactly when
(A) φ is surjective. (B) G/N is finite. (C) H is abelian. (D) N = ker φ. (E) N = {e}.

solution.text:
The map is well-defined by φ¯(gN) = φ(g) because φ kills N . Its kernel consists of the
cosets in (ker φ)/N. This kernel is trivial exactly when ker φ = N. Its image remains im φ,
so injectivity of the induced map does not require surjectivity onto H.

question.text:

(A) G is abelian.
(B) N is contained in the center of G.
